description:
From the fz-kdt.119 cold review (2026-09-01). The review's
FZ_DEBUG_TUPLE_SHAPE probe -- a runtime counter firing when a value
passes an arm's test while lying outside the surface that arm's body
was compiled for -- found TEN fixtures in one corpus pass (00183 x16,
00230 x16, 00418 x4, 00419 x16, 00420 x81, hof_three_distinct x6,
predicate_search x7, take_drop_split x81, receive_map_pattern x1,
unused_range_binding x4). The static fz-kdt.129 gate sees 19 pairwise
escapes on 14 hand-picked fixtures; this sees the real thing, on the
production path, corpus-wide, cheaply. Land it as a permanent
env-gated tripwire (FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP: count, or
hard-error under the flag) + a corpus sweep recipe. This is the
fourth demonstration that corpus stdout sweeps pass while dispatch
defects ship -- this instrument is the corrective. fz-kdt.119 lands
it in-story per its gate list; this ticket tracks the corpus-sweep
integration and the triage of the ten findings (each is a latent
blind-routing site; the two x81 are the take_drop blocker ticket).

comments.text:
IN-STORY HALF LANDED at fz-kdt.119 (4ca1dc7e7): FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP is a permanent env-gated tripwire in runtime_type_predicate::surface_membership, documented in .agent/docs/dispatch-matrix.md (### The dynamic tripwire). What remains here is the corpus-sweep integration and the triage.

MECHANISM, which is sharper than the review's probe. The interpreter answers each dispatch type test as the three lowerings do -- PositionScope::Lowered, blind exactly where they are blind -- and the tripwire then re-asks the tuple axis under PositionScope::Full, which looks at the positions they skip. A value admitted by the first reading and refused by the second passed a test no shape of the arm's surface names. Off unless the var is set; 'abort' makes each finding fatal (bisect one fixture down to a dispatch); anything else reports each on stderr. Census recipe:

  FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP=1 fz2 interp <fixture> 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -c 'surface-membership escape'

BASELINE, pinned at the landing (584 fixtures, interp): SEVEN fixtures, 268 occurrences.

  00183_enum_take_list_range     16
  00230_enum_take_chained        16
  00418_enum_count_range          4
  00419_enum_take_mixed          16
  00420_enum_take_drop_split    106
  enum_take_drop_split          106
  unused_range_binding            4

Every one is a nested LIST position -- the Scope-A carve-out, blind on purpose -- and the two at 106 are the same program reached by two paths: that is the fz-kdt.132 population. LATENT SITES, not regressions; a ratchet like the 19-escape census, and a new entry wants a ticket rather than a re-blessed number.

Three of the review's ten are CLOSED by fz-kdt.119 itself, because their blind routing went through tuple positions the test can now see: hof_three_distinct (x6), enum_predicate_search (x7), receive_map_pattern (x1).

NOTE ON COMPARABILITY: this instrument has no reading before fz-kdt.119. Without per-position shapes there is no record of what an arm's surface named, so there is nothing to compare a value against. The review's FZ_DEBUG_TUPLE_SHAPE counted something else (its experimental partial check missing), which is why 00420 reads 106 here against the review's 81 -- different instruments, same population.

Scope correction from the fz-kdt.119 refutation: the landed tripwire's Full re-ask un-blinds WHICH positions are asked, not what the LIST axis can see -- it cannot detect list-ELEMENT escapes (measured: a program misrouting [:p,:q] into a [integer] body reports 0). The earlier 'sees the real thing corpus-wide' claim is over-broad: it sees the TUPLE axis corpus-wide. The 19-escape static census remains the only list-element instrument until fz-kdt.107 step 3 gives lists element discrimination.

title: A dynamic surface-membership tripwire: the instrument the dispatch class has been missing
